questions.subject: LSTM
questions.question: What is GRU in LSTM and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: GRU in LSTM refers to gated recurrent unit. It works by simplified LSTM variant. Key characteristics include update gate, reset gate; no separate cell state. Example: z_t = sigmoid(W_z · [h_{t-1}, x_t]); r_t = sigmoid(W_r · [h_{t-1}, x_t]). Common pitfalls include LSTM vs GRU performance.

questions.question: Explain the difference between LSTM cell and GRU in LSTM.
questions.ideal_answer: LSTM cell and GRU differ in several ways: LSTM cell is long short-term memory (works by gated recurrent architecture) whereas GRU is gated recurrent unit (works by simplified LSTM variant). LSTM cell is typically used for forget gate, input gate, output gate, cell state, while GRU is used for update gate, reset gate; no separate cell state. Example demonstrating LSTM cell: f_t = sigmoid(W_f · [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_f). Example demonstrating GRU: z_t = sigmoid(W_z · [h_{t-1}, x_t]); r_t = sigmoid(W_r · [h_{t-1}, x_t]).

questions.question: Explain the difference between LSTM cell and cell state in LSTM.
questions.ideal_answer: LSTM cell and cell state differ in several ways: LSTM cell is long short-term memory (works by gated recurrent architecture) whereas cell state is memory highway (works by linear information flow). LSTM cell is typically used for forget gate, input gate, output gate, cell state, while cell state is used for additive updates, minimal gradient flow obstruction. Example demonstrating LSTM cell: f_t = sigmoid(W_f · [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_f). Example demonstrating cell state: C_t = f_t * C_{t-1} + i_t * tanh(W_C · [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_C).
